questions.stem: A 35 year old teacher has a 3 day history of a hoarse voice, sore throat, runny nose and a dry cough. Several pupils have had colds. She does not smoke. Her temperature is 37.5°C, pulse rate 80 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 99% breathing air. There is no stridor.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: URTI affects the nose, sinuses, pharynx and larynx, so hoarseness with coryza and sore throat is a viral URTI.

steps.x: Acute **coryza** with **hoarseness** after contacts: the larynx is part of the upper tract.

elim: Drooling, stridor and a toxic patient.
Chronic hoarseness with heartburn, not coryza.
Hoarseness for weeks in a smoker, not a 3 day coryzal illness.
Chronic hoarseness from voice overuse, no fever or coryza.

steps.x: **D. Viral upper respiratory tract infection.** URTI includes nose, sinuses, pharynx and larynx.

questions.stem: An 18 month old boy had a runny nose for 2 days. Tonight he woke with a barking cough and a hoarse cry. His temperature is 37.9°C, pulse rate 138 bpm, respiratory rate 36 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air. He is not drooling.
questions.q: Which is the most likely finding on auscultation of the airway?
questions.e: Croup causes a harsh inspiratory stridor from laryngeal obstruction, with a barking cough.

steps.x: **Barking cough** in a toddler after coryza: **croup**.

elim: Small airway narrowing, as in asthma or viral wheeze.
A sign of respiratory distress in neonates, not of laryngeal obstruction.

steps.x: **D. Harsh inspiratory stridor.** Croup = stridor (harsh inspiratory sound).

questions.stem: A 4 year old girl has had a cold for 2 days. Since this evening she has a seal-like cough, a hoarse voice and noisy breathing in when upset. Her temperature is 38.0°C, pulse rate 124 bpm and oxygen saturation 96% breathing air. She is talking, swallowing and not drooling. Her chest is clear.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: A barking cough, hoarseness and stridor after a cold in a child aged 6 months to 6 years is croup, usually parainfluenza.

steps.x: Toddler, coryza, **barking cough**, **stridor**, not toxic.

elim: High fever and a toxic child.
Drooling, unable to swallow, toxic, no barking cough.
Sudden choking onset without a preceding cold.
Expiratory wheeze, not barking cough and stridor.

steps.x: **B. Croup.** Croup: 6 months to 6 years, parainfluenza.

questions.stem: A 9 year old boy has a 3 day history of fever, sore throat and red, watery eyes. Several children at his swimming club have the same illness. His temperature is 38.4°C and pulse rate 104 bpm. His pharynx is red, both conjunctivae are injected, and he has tender preauricular nodes.
questions.q: Which is the most likely causative organism?
questions.e: Pharyngitis with conjunctivitis and fever, spread in swimming pools, is typical of adenovirus.

steps.x: **Sore throat + conjunctivitis + pool**: adenovirus.

elim: Abrupt fever and myalgia, not conjunctivitis.
Causes the common cold, not conjunctivitis.

steps.x: **A. Adenovirus.** URTI viruses: rhinovirus, coronavirus, adenovirus, influenza.

questions.stem: A 41 year old man has had a sudden onset of fever, aching muscles, headache, dry cough and sore throat since yesterday. It is January and several colleagues are off sick. His temperature is 39.2°C, pulse rate 104 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air. His chest is clear.
questions.q: Which is the most likely causative organism?
questions.e: Abrupt high fever with myalgia in winter outbreaks is influenza, one of the main URTI viruses.

clues: sudden onset of fever, aching muscles
steps.x: **Abrupt**, **myalgia**, high fever, winter: influenza.

elim: Gradual onset with lower respiratory symptoms.
Milder coryza without high fever and myalgia.

steps.x: **B. Influenza virus.** Influenza is a URTI virus; winter is a risk factor.

questions.stem: A 27 year old nursery worker has a 2 day history of sneezing, a runny nose, sore throat and mild cough. It is December. She is otherwise well and takes no medication. Her temperature is 37.4°C, pulse rate 78 bpm. Her throat is red and her chest is clear.
questions.q: Which factor in her history most increases her risk of this condition?
o: Close contact with infected children in winter
questions.e: URTI risk factors are the winter season and contact with infected individuals.

steps.x: **Winter** and **contact** with children.

elim: Not described and not a main risk factor.

steps.x: **A. Close contact with infected children in winter.** Risk: winter season, contact with infected people.

questions.stem: A 33 year old man has a 3 day history of a sore throat, blocked nose and dry cough. His temperature is 37.6°C, pulse rate 82 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air. His GP suspects a viral upper respiratory tract infection and examines him.
questions.q: Which is the most likely finding on examination?
o: Bronchial breathing at the right base
Stony dull percussion at the left base
questions.e: URTI examination shows an erythematous throat and nasal congestion with no focal chest findings.

steps.x: Expect **a red throat** and **nothing in the chest**.
**C. Erythematous pharynx.** Exam: erythematous throat, nasal congestion, no focal chest signs.

questions.stem: A 38 year old woman had a cold 11 days ago. Her runny nose initially improved, but she now has pain over both cheeks that is worse bending forward, a blocked nose and thick green nasal discharge. Her temperature is 38.1°C and pulse rate 90 bpm. Both maxillae are tender.
questions.q: Which is the most likely complication?
questions.e: Viral mucosal damage and impaired clearance allow secondary bacterial infection of the sinuses after a URTI.

steps.x: Cold, **improvement then worsening**, facial pain.

elim: Ear pain and a bulging drum.
Would be localised, not bilateral with nasal discharge.
Brief electric shocks, no discharge or fever.

steps.x: **D. Secondary bacterial sinusitis.** Secondary bacterial complications: sinusitis or otitis media.

questions.stem: A 58 year old man has had a cold for 4 days. He is managing at home with paracetamol. His temperature is 37.8°C, pulse rate 84 bpm and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air. He asks which new symptoms should prompt him to seek urgent review.
questions.q: Which new feature would most suggest progression to pneumonia?
questions.e: High fever, breathlessness or chest pain are emergency features suggesting progression to a lower respiratory tract infection.

clues: which new symptoms should prompt him to seek urgent review
steps.x: Red flags: **high fever**, **breathlessness**, **chest pain**.
**B. Breathlessness with chest pain.** Breathlessness or chest pain after a cold: think LRTI.

questions.stem: A 72 year old man has a 3 day history of sore throat, sneezing, runny nose and a dry cough. He has no breathlessness or chest pain. His temperature is 37.6°C, pulse rate 80 bpm, BP 134/82 mmHg, respiratory rate 15 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air. His throat is red and his chest is clear.
questions.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.e: Coryza, sore throat, dry cough and low-grade fever with a clear chest is a viral URTI, even in an older patient.

clues: His throat is red and his chest is clear
steps.x: Coryzal symptoms, low fever, **no focal chest signs**.

elim: He has no known COPD or increased breathlessness.
No focal signs, normal respiratory rate and saturation.

steps.x: **E. Viral upper respiratory tract infection.** URTI: no focal chest findings.

questions.stem: A 3 year old girl had a cold with a runny nose for 4 days. Last night she became feverish and irritable and has been crying and pulling at her left ear. Her temperature is 38.6°C and pulse rate 136 bpm. Her throat is red.
questions.q: Which is the most likely finding on otoscopy?
o: Retracted dull drum with fluid level
questions.e: Viral damage and Eustachian tube dysfunction allow secondary bacterial otitis media after a URTI, giving a bulging red drum.

clues: cold with a runny nose for 4 days
steps.x: After a cold, **ear pain and fever**: acute otitis media.

elim: Fever and ear pulling after a cold suggest otitis media.
Chronic suppurative otitis media, not an acute illness.
Otitis media with effusion, usually painless.

steps.x: **A. Bulging red left tympanic membrane.** Secondary bacterial complications: otitis media.

questions.stem: A 46 year old woman has a 4 day history of runny nose, sore throat and cough. Her GP is deciding whether she has an upper respiratory tract infection or pneumonia. Her temperature is 37.7°C.
questions.q: Which finding would most support an upper respiratory tract infection?
o: Bronchial breathing at the right base
No focal chest signs with normal oxygen saturation
Respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute
questions.e: URTI has no focal chest findings; breathlessness, chest pain or abnormal chest signs suggest pneumonia.

clues: upper respiratory tract infection or pneumonia
steps.x: URTI: the **chest is clear**.
**B. No focal chest signs with normal oxygen saturation.** No focal chest findings in URTI.

questions.stem: A 69 year old man has had a cold for 5 days. Since yesterday he has a temperature of 38.9°C, breathlessness and left-sided chest pain on inspiration. His pulse rate is 108 bpm, BP 118/72 mmHg, respiratory rate 26 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 91% breathing air. There are crackles at the left base.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to exclude pneumonia?
questions.e: In severe cases, blood tests and a chest X-ray are used to exclude pneumonia.

steps.x: Red flags of **LRTI**: image the chest.

elim: For suspected PE; fever and crackles point to infection.
He is severely unwell with red flags.

steps.x: **A. Chest X-ray.** Severe cases: bloods and chest X-ray to exclude pneumonia.

questions.stem: A 2 year old boy has a barking cough, hoarse voice and stridor only when crying after 2 days of coryza. His temperature is 37.8°C, pulse rate 128 bpm, respiratory rate 30 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air. He is alert and drinking.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation?
o: Throat examination with a tongue depressor
Viral PCR of a nasopharyngeal swab
questions.e: Croup, like other URTIs, is a clinical diagnosis.

steps.x: Typical mild croup: **clinical**.

elim: Not used routinely; may distress the child.
Avoid in stridor; could precipitate obstruction if epiglottitis.

steps.x: **C. No investigation required.** URTI (including croup) is a clinical diagnosis.

questions.stem: A 30 year old man has a 2 day history of sore throat, sneezing, runny nose and a dry cough. His temperature is 37.4°C, pulse rate 76 bpm and oxygen saturation 99% breathing air. His throat is red and his chest is clear. He asks for a test to find out which virus he has.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate way to make the diagnosis?
o: Clinical diagnosis from history and examination
Viral PCR of a nasal swab
questions.e: The gold standard for URTI remains clinical diagnosis.

clues: His throat is red and his chest is clear
steps.x: Mild, typical: **clinical**.

elim: Not routinely needed; the virus does not change management.

steps.x: **C. Clinical diagnosis from history and examination.** URTI: clinical diagnosis is the gold standard.

questions.stem: A 64 year old woman with a 4 day cold has a temperature of 38.3°C and feels breathless walking upstairs. Her pulse rate is 96 bpm, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 95% breathing air. Her chest is clear on auscultation. Blood tests and a chest X-ray (see item resources) are taken to exclude pneumonia.

visual.title: Chest X-ray
visual.caption: Clear lung fields: no consolidation, effusion or cavitation.

questions.q: Which is the most likely finding on the chest X-ray?
questions.e: URTI does not involve the lungs; with no focal chest findings the X-ray is expected to be clear.

clues: Her chest is clear on auscultation
steps.x: No focal signs: expect **no focal X-ray change**.
**B. Clear lung fields.** URTI: no focal chest findings; CXR to exclude pneumonia.

questions.stem: A 25 year old woman has a 2 day history of sore throat, runny nose and cough. She is eating and drinking. Her temperature is 37.5°C, pulse rate 78 bpm and oxygen saturation 99% breathing air. Her throat is red and her chest is clear. She starts paracetamol and ibuprofen.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate safety-net advice?
o: Attend A&E if still coryzal tomorrow
Return after 3 weeks if not better
Return for a chest X-ray in 1 week
Return if not improving in 3 to 4 days
Start antibiotics if the discharge turns green
questions.e: Self-care with paracetamol and ibuprofen and review in 3 to 4 days if not improving; most URTIs resolve within about a week.

steps.x: Self-care, then **review at 3 to 4 days**.

elim: Discharge colour does not indicate bacteria.

steps.x: **D. Return if not improving in 3 to 4 days.** Self-care, review in 3-4 days if not improving.

questions.stem: A 39 year old man has a 3 day history of a cold with a severely blocked nose that is stopping him sleeping. He is otherwise well and is taking paracetamol. His temperature is 37.3°C, pulse rate 74 bpm. His nasal mucosa is swollen and his chest is clear.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate additional treatment for his symptoms?
questions.e: Nasal decongestants such as xylometazoline can help nasal congestion in a URTI.

steps.x: Problem is **congestion**: a **decongestant**.

elim: Not for an acute viral cold.

steps.x: **E. Xylometazoline nasal spray.** Nasal decongestants (xylometazoline) can help.

questions.stem: A 44 year old woman had a cold 9 days ago. She now has a very sore throat, fever and pus on both tonsils with tender anterior cervical nodes and no cough. Her GP suspects a secondary bacterial infection. Her temperature is 38.6°C. She has no allergies.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate antibiotic?
questions.e: When a bacterial cause is suspected, phenoxymethylpenicillin (penicillin V) is used.

steps.x: Bacterial suspected, **no allergy**.

elim: Not first-line, and causes a rash if the cause is EBV.

steps.x: **E. Phenoxymethylpenicillin.** Bacterial: penicillin V.

questions.stem: A 52 year old man with a URTI has developed a severe bacterial throat infection with exudate and fever of 38.7°C. He developed facial swelling and wheeze after phenoxymethylpenicillin 5 years ago. He takes no regular medication. His GP decides to prescribe an antibiotic.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate antibiotic?
questions.e: Clarithromycin is the alternative to penicillin V in penicillin allergy.

clues: facial swelling and wheeze after phenoxymethylpenicillin
steps.x: **Penicillin allergy**: a macrolide.

elim: Cross-reactivity risk after an anaphylactic-type reaction.

steps.x: **C. Clarithromycin.** Penicillin allergy: clarithromycin.

questions.stem: A 31 year old man has a 3 day history of runny nose, sore throat and cough producing a little green phlegm. He asks for antibiotics because the phlegm is green. His temperature is 37.6°C, pulse rate 80 bpm, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute and oxygen saturation 98% breathing air. His chest is clear.
questions.q: Which is the most appropriate management?
questions.e: A viral URTI is managed with self-care and simple analgesia; antibiotics only if a bacterial cause is suspected.

steps.x: Viral URTI, well: **self-care**.

elim: No chest signs or red flags.
Green phlegm alone does not mean bacteria.

steps.x: **E. Self-care with paracetamol and ibuprofen.** Paracetamol and ibuprofen; review in 3-4 days.

questions.stem: A 26 year old woman has a 2 day history of a streaming nose, blocked nostrils and a sore throat after her partner had a cold. Her temperature is 37.3°C. A student asks what causes the runny, blocked nose.
questions.q: Which is the most likely mechanism?
o: CSF leak through the cribriform plate
Loss of nasal cilia from smoking
Viral inflammation causing mucosal oedema and increased mucus secretion
questions.e: Respiratory viruses infect the nasal and pharyngeal mucosa, causing local inflammation, oedema and increased mucus secretion.

clues: after her partner had a cold
steps.x: Virus infects mucosa: **inflammation, oedema, mucus**.

elim: She is not described as a smoker.

steps.x: **E. Viral inflammation causing mucosal oedema and increased mucus secretion.** URTI: inflammation, oedema, increased mucus.

questions.stem: A 3 year old boy with parainfluenza virus infection has a barking cough and inspiratory stridor. His temperature is 37.9°C and oxygen saturation 97% breathing air. A lateral neck X-ray taken elsewhere shows narrowing just below the vocal cords.
questions.q: Which is the main site of inflammation causing his symptoms?
questions.e: Croup is laryngotracheal inflammation with subglottic narrowing, producing a barking cough and inspiratory stridor.

clues: narrowing just below the vocal cords
steps.x: **Subglottic** narrowing: laryngotracheal.

elim: Gives crackles and hypoxia, not stridor.

steps.x: **D. Larynx and trachea.** Croup = laryngotracheobronchitis with subglottic narrowing.

questions.stem: A 5 year old girl develops ear pain and fever 4 days after a cold. Otoscopy shows a bulging red tympanic membrane. Her temperature is 38.5°C. Her mother asks how a cold in the nose has reached the ear.
questions.q: Which is the most likely route of infection?
o: Spread through a perforated drum from outside
questions.e: Viral mucosal damage and impaired clearance allow nasopharyngeal bacteria to reach the middle ear via the Eustachian tube.

steps.x: Nose to middle ear: the **Eustachian tube**.

elim: The drum is intact and bulging.

steps.x: **D. Spread through the Eustachian tube.** Secondary otitis media via the Eustachian tube.

questions.stem: A 34 year old man develops facial pain and purulent nasal discharge 10 days after a viral URTI. His temperature is 38.0°C. A student asks why a viral infection has led to a bacterial sinus infection.
questions.q: Which is the most likely mechanism?
questions.e: Viral damage to the mucosa and impaired mucociliary clearance allow bacteria to invade the sinuses.

steps.x: The virus **damages mucosa** and **impairs clearance**.
**D. Viral mucosal damage impairing clearance.** Secondary bacterial infection follows mucosal damage.

questions.stem: A 29 year old woman has a viral upper respiratory tract infection. She has been taking only paracetamol. Her temperature is 37.4°C on day 2 and her symptoms have gone by day 7. A student asks why she improved without antibiotics.
questions.q: Which best explains her recovery?
o: The host immune response clears the virus
The virus becomes dormant in nerves
questions.e: URTIs are self-limiting, resolving in about a week, driven by the host immune response rather than ongoing tissue damage.

steps.x: **Self-limiting**: immunity clears it within a **week**.

elim: No routine vaccine covers most URTI viruses.

steps.x: **D. The host immune response clears the virus.** URTIs resolve in about 1 week via the host immune response.
